markdown_content: ## Two-Way Zippers in Clo: Feature Overview This section explains the new two-way zipper feature in Clo, detailing how it enables the simulation of zippers with two sliders and pullers, commonly used in bags and garments. Key terms include zipper slider, puller, tape, teeth, and zipper types (one-way, two-way). The two-way zipper feature in Clo allows users to add and simulate zippers with two sliders and pullers, a common design in bags and some garments. Traditionally, many bags have two zipper sliders that can open and close from either end, and this feature replicates that functionality digitally. To use the feature, you select the zipper slider and puller component, **not** the tape or teeth. The property editor in Clo only shows the two-way zipper option when the slider and puller are selected. Selecting the tape or teeth will not display this option. ## Configuring Two-Way Zippers This section covers step-by-step instructions for enabling and customizing two-way zippers, including zipper orientation options and editing capabilities within Clo. Once the zipper slider and puller are selected, the user can change the zipper type to "two-way" in the property editor. Two orientation options are available: - **Bottom to bottom:** Both sliders start from the bottom ends. - **Head to head:** Both sliders start from the top ends, ideal for bags with zippers meeting at the top. Both sliders remain fully functional and editable. Users can move sliders independently around the zipper tape, adjust zipper gauge, and modify sliders and pullers as needed. Typically, sliders and pullers remain consistent on a zipper to maintain design integrity. ## Simulation and Interaction Features This section explains how the two-way zipper behaves during simulation, including unzip functionality and practical applications. The two-way zippers in Clo are fully interactive during simulation. Users can unzip the zipper by pulling the sliders apart, mimicking real-life zipper operation. This allows realistic visualization, such as opening a bag to reveal contents. The unzip feature works seamlessly regardless of zipper position, allowing partial or full unzipping. This flexibility supports various garment and accessory designs without notable limitations. ## Compatibility and Limitations This brief section summarizes the compatibility of the two-way zipper feature and any known constraints. The two-way zipper feature works on all garment types supported by Clo. Switching zipper types is straightforward; users can toggle between one-way and two-way zipper configurations at any time without losing zipper settings. There are no significant limitations mentioned, making the feature simple to use and widely applicable in virtual garment design.
